title: Terraform module: private storage primitives (EBS, EFS, S3) with snapshots, KMS defaults, lifecycle and health checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a production-ready Terraform module that standardizes how Private (VPC) deployments create and manage block/file/object storage across AWS: EBS volumes for VM-backed instances, EFS for shared mounts, and S3 buckets for object artifacts and backups. The module will enforce default encryption, tenant-scoped KMS key support, snapshot lifecycle policies, cross-account-safe tagging, and an ops-friendly health-checking surface (CloudWatch metrics + SNS alerts).

Scope and constraints: Module must be usable as a single composition (redwood_storage_private) and also allow per-resource submodules. Defaults are secure-by-default (SSE-KMS for S3, encrypted EBS with CMK, EFS encrypted, snapshot lifecycle retention of 30 days). Support opt-out flags for customers with existing CMKs or compliance needs. Avoid resource name collisions across accounts and support tagging conventions for cost and audit. The module must be Terraform 1.5+ compatible and publish a clear upgrade path for stateful resources (especially EBS volume->snapshot naming and S3 bucket lifecycle changes).
acceptance_criteria:
- Module published under modules/terraform/redwood_storage_private with versioned releases and CHANGELOG entries.
- Exposed inputs: prefix, environment, kms_key_arn (optional), enable_cross_account_snapshots (bool), snapshot_retention_days (int), s3_lifecycle_rules (map/string), tags (map).
- Defaults: EBS and EFS encrypted with generated CMK when kms_key_arn not provided; S3 default SSE-KMS with object lock off by default.
- Automated CloudWatch alarms for failed snapshot operations, low EBS snapshot success rate, and EFS lifecycle errors; alarms publish to SNS topic configurable by module consumer.
- Integration test: example/private-deploy-demo applies in a sandbox and creates resources, runs a snapshot rotation job, and verifies alarms fire on simulated failures.
- Security review completed and documented in PRD/Confluence with KMS key policy samples for cross-account restores.
- Documentation: usage examples for single-tenant and multi-tenant patterns, migration notes for existing buckets/volumes, and breaking-change guidance for upgrades.
comments: 2026-02-26: Kickoff sync with infra and security. Decision: secure-by-default with optional override for customer-managed CMKs. Action: Markus to draft KMS policy templates.

2026-03-02: Prototype module created (WIP) — submodules for ebs/efs/s3 implemented. Found issue: S3 bucket naming collisions in org accounts; plan to add deterministic prefixing using account_id and region.

2026-03-04: Review feedback from Security (Elena): require explicit kms_key_arn for high-compliance customers, and module should not auto-create keys when security_review_required=true in parent org. Marked as TODO in README.
2026-03-07: Engineering review: added CloudWatch metric filters and SNS topic arn input. Decision to default snapshot_retention_days=30 and make rotation cron configurable by cron_expression input.

2026-03-11: Ops requested health-check Lambda option to validate latest snapshot age and snapshot consistency across AZs. Lambda is optional, insulated behind a boolean flag to avoid extra infra cost in low-tier accounts.
2026-03-12: Draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/482. CI failing on acceptance tests due to EFS mount target quotas in sandbox — workaround: throttle parallelism in tests.

2026-03-13: Next steps: finish PR feedback, add explicit state-migration notes for renaming default lifecycle rules to avoid forcing new buckets, and prepare Confluence doc link for security review. Target merge before 2026-03-20.
